drugRefs.dose: Cephalexin 500 mg PO q6h or Amoxicillin-clavulanate 875/125 mg PO q12h
drugRefs.why: Mild infections without deep tissue involvement can be treated with narrow-spectrum oral agents targeting staphylococci and streptococci.
Broader coverage including gram-negatives and anaerobes is warranted for deep, limb-threatening, or systemically significant infections.

drugRefs.dose: Clindamycin 450 mg PO q8h + Ciprofloxacin 500 mg PO q12h
drugRefs.coverage: Alternative combination covering gram-positives, gram-negatives, and anaerobes in penicillin-allergic patients.

drugRefs.regimenLabel: Vancomycin (if MRSA risk) added to above regimens
drugRefs.coverage: Added when MRSA risk factors are present (prior MRSA, prolonged hospitalization, recent broad-spectrum antibiotics).

coverageMatrix.completeness: Coverage should be matched to wound severity - broad empiric coverage for all wounds is over-treatment for mild infections.
gaps: Osteomyelitis requires bone biopsy/culture for truly targeted, often prolonged therapy - empiric coverage alone is insufficient if bone is involved.

stewardship.deescalation: Once deep tissue/bone culture results return, narrow to the most targeted agent(s) covering the confirmed organism(s), and reassess duration based on whether bone is involved (longer course) or soft tissue alone (shorter course).

framework: Do not treat clinically uninfected ulcers with antibiotics - colonization without clinical signs of infection (erythema, warmth, purulence, pain) is not an indication for treatment.
Match spectrum to severity (IDSA/IWGDF mild/moderate/severe classification) rather than using broad-spectrum coverage for all diabetic foot wounds by default.
Obtain deep tissue or bone culture (not superficial swab) whenever possible before starting therapy, since superficial swabs often reflect colonizing rather than infecting organisms.
